topics.title: Laws of superposition and faunal succession

questions.text: (a) Discuss the interior of earth in detail. Also describe the processes (10) involved in the formation of igneous rocks. (b) What are laws of superposition and faunal succession? Describe (10) (20) classification and nomenclature of stratigraphic units in detail.
Elaborate various laws of stratigraphy, use suitable sketches/examples in support (20) of your answer.
(a) Describe various modes of fossilization. (15) (b) Briefly describe various lithostratigraphic units. (5)
What categories of information we depict from the fossils found in sedimentary strata? (20) Give examples. Describe some of common processes of fossilization.

(a) What are main types of sedimentary rocks and how are they formed? (10) Also describe the classification scheme of these sedimentary rocks in detail. (b) Discuss optical properties of common rock-forming minerals in detail. (10) (20)

topics.title: Physical and optical properties of the common silicate and non-silicate mineral groups

questions.text: Elaborate the fundamental silica tetrahedral structure (SiO 4 ). Give possibilities of (20) SiO 4 linkage to give rise to six silicate structural groups.
Describe structure of neso silicates. Also draw its sketch. Narrate physical and optical (20) properties of olivine group of minerals.

Mountain Belts are made of several mountain ranges, usually with related histories. (20) There are some familiar mountain ranges of the world, mention simply their names and localities. However, discuss in detail the tectonic frame work of Himalayas.
Discuss in detail the concept and terminology of faults. Discuss criteria for (20) identification of faults.

(a) Write down the genetic classification of faults. Also relate principal stresses with (10) all those faults. (b) Briefly describe the various types of plate boundaries and the associated earth (10) features along them.
What is the difference between fracture and joints? Discuss importance of fracture (20) and joint analysis.
Outline important events of Indian Plate drift and subsequent tectonics from Mesozoic (20) onwards in Pakistan region. Draw sketches.

Earth scientists are aware of the fact that metamorphism and plate tectonics are (20) intimately linked and are responsible for the development of different metamorphic facies. Explain with diagram(s) the type of plate tectonic boundary and formation of the related facies.
Describe the principal of plate tectonic with evidences. Explain the Wilson cycle (20) in detail.
Write comprehensive note on the following topics. (10 each) (20) (a) Tectonic framework of Pakistan (b) Geothermal energy resource potentials of Pakistan
Explain the tectonic framework of Pakistan with an example of Indian-Eurasian (20) and Indian-African plate drifting.
Describe the test compositions of order Foraminiferida. Discuss their ecology and (20) how it plays important role in Tertiary biostratigraphy.

(a) Describe various sedimentary structures of the clastic rocks. Also write (10) down their importance in the field. (b) Describe various types of volcanic material and their characteristic features. (10)

topics.title: Composition
analysis: Appearances: 4  |  Years: 2016, 2018, 2019, 2021  |  Demands: Explain/Elucidate (1), Describe (1), Discuss (1)
Recurring terms: composition (4), minerals (3), earth (2), mention (2), chemical (2)
Pattern: No strong command-word shift is visible between the earlier and later parts of the supplied series (0% vs 0% analytical/critical wording).

questions.text: Classify pyroxene group of minerals based on chemical composition. Also (20) mention their physical and optical properties.
What are Pegmatites? Discuss the texture and mineralogical composition of (20) pegmatites. What precious minerals are associated with acidic pegmatites?
(a) Briefly describe internal structure and composition of the earth. (10) (b) What do you know about Isostasy and Isostatic Adjustment? Explain. (10)

Global society is heavily dependent on minerals and metals. Earth is the source of all (20) these resources. All minerals are grouped into silicate and non-silicate minerals, and further are divided into seven major classes according to their economic use. For example, class Sulfides has mineral Galena whose chemical formula is PbF, and is a source of LEAD. Make a Table of four columns; 1st column should carry the title ‘Minerals Class’, 2nd column ‘the Names of Minerals of the classes’, 3rd column is Chemical formulae of minerals of 2 nd column, 4th column the economic use of minerals of column-2. Mention 10 minerals in that Table, giving their class (1st column), mineral name (2nd column), chemical composition (3rd column), and economic use (4th column).
What are igneous rocks? Give in short, the mineralogical and textural (20) classification of igneous rocks.
Describe development of different types of metamorphic facies during subduction (20) process. With the help of temperature-pressure diagram, elaborate regimes of metamorphic facies.

topics.title: Optical properties of opaque and non-opaque minerals in plane polarized light and under crossed nicol including metallic under reflected light

questions.text: Describe Polarized Light Microscopy along with optical properties of opaque and (20) non-opaque mineral? How to identify the Gout crystal and Pseudo-Gout?
What are the merits and demerits of refraction seismology, magnetic surveying, (20) resistivity surveying and gravity to probe the depth of bedrock, bedrock lithology and crustal thickness?

questions.text: What methods of geophysical exploration are used for metallic ore deposits? What (20) instruments are used for acquisition and interpretation of data?

(a) What is Walther’s law of superposition? Discuss concepts and (10) significance of sequence stratigraphy. (b) Describe “Upper Indus basin with respect to its hydrocarbon potentials” (10) (20) in detail.

topics.title: Application of geophysical methods for site investigation
analysis: Appearances: 2  |  Years: 2019, 2022  |  Demands: Write note(s) (1), Explain/Elucidate (1)

questions.text: Explain different geophysical methods such as gravity, magnetic, electrical (20) resistivity, electromagnetic and seismic. Explain the application of each method, its strength and its limitations.

Differentiate between volcanic and fissure eruptions. Describe types of materials (20) exhaled by volcanoes. How these materials are hazardous to men and environment?
Discuss the geological conditions that normally trigger land sliding in northern (20) Pakistan. Describe some of the measures to mitigate its effects.

Pakistan has plenty mineral resources. Massive sulfide bodies are also found in (20) different places. Electromagnetic geophysical methods is considered most suitable for the exploration of such high electrical conductivity bodies buried under surface. Discuss in detail the electromagnetic method, the controlling factors for increasing depth penetration and its other applications.
What characteristics a sedimentary strata should contain to be designated as a (20) “Formation”? How the formation is divided into sub-units? Describe the characters of Salt Range Formation.

Weathering is a natural process to break down the rocks and the minerals. This process (20) involves a set of physical, chemical, and biological processes. Explain different types of physical and chemical weathering, and describe the role of water in chemical weathering process.
